newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - France seeks joint French bid for Thomson-CSF.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - France seeks joint French bid for Thomson-CSF.

text.p: The French government is urging rivals Alcatel Alsthom and Lagardere to bury the hatchet and bid jointly for Thomson-CSF to create a French defence electronics giant with global aspirations.
It also made clear on Thursday that it was looking for future defence industry partners in Europe, but that bids that would leave the company in non-French hands would not be welcome.

"The government isn't imposing a marriage on them (Alcatel and Lagardere) but this is what it has asked the chairmen of these companies to do," said a government official, confirming reports that Prime Minister Alain Juppe was looking for a joint offer.
Alcatel and Lagardere have been at loggerheads since the government failed last year in its first attempt to privatise Thomson-CSF's parent -- the Thomson SA group.
"We need to reinforce the defence electronics industry ...especially when you consider the huge concentration taking place across the Atlantic," the official said, speaking on condition of anonymity.
He said the government planned to use the privatisation of its 58-percent stake in Thomson-CSF initially as an opportunity to group together the main French defence players.
"During this first phase, the French companies can indicate who their allies are within the European industry," he said. But he said the plan was to forge European links at a later stage.
The French government is not open, he said, to a purely foreign offer, even from a European company such as Britain's GEC Plc which has ties to both Lagardere and Alcatel.
"A 100 percent GEC, and purely GEC, offer doesn't correspond to the French industry restructuring we envisage," he said.

Joint Alcatel-Lagardere control of Thomson-CSF "will only work if they're willing, which is why the government isn't imposing this condition. It's up to them to see if they're capable of making a joint offer," said the official.

A spokesman for Alcatel declined to comment on the possibility of a joint bid but recalled chairman Serge Tchuruk's recent remarks that it would be unwise to have too many "contradictory interests" represented on Thomson-CSF's board.

Tchuruk told the newspaper Le Monde two weeks ago that he did not feel "entrenched or aggressive" toward Lagardere but that a controlling shareholder was needed at Thomson-CSF to carry out a restructuring of the French electronics industry.

"Lagardere hasn't said so, but they feel the same way," said analyst Bernard Angeniol at brokerage Schelcher Prince. "It would be lovely if everyone could get along nicely, but that will be hard," he said.

"It looks really difficult given the poor quality of relations between them," said another Paris analyst. He said fierce antagonism had developed between the two companies since they emerged as the two rivals for the Thomson group last year.
"The war between them just keeps intensifying," he said.
Officials at Lagardere, whose interests range from publishing to missiles, were not available for comment.

The government originally said it preferred Lagardere's offer for Thomson, but the sale plan fell through in December after the Privatisation Commission objected to the terms, notably for the sale of Thomson SA's other subsidiary, Thomson Multimedia (TMM), to South Korea's Daewoo Electronics.
The government changed its approach and decided to sell Thomson's two businesses separately.
